note: Hand-graded behavior specification, not a `claude plugin eval` suite. Ids 5 to 12 belonged to the commit and pr skills and stay unused.
how_to_run: Run specs/setup-fixture.sh <dir> to build a scratch clone with a local bare origin. Before each eval, put the clone in the state its prompt names in parentheses; setup-fixture.sh leaves it clean on main and prints the commands. Start one fresh headless session per eval inside the clone with `claude --plugin-dir <plugin repo> --allowedTools 'Bash(git *)' -p '<prompt>'`, then grade the transcript and the git state against the expectations. For eval 19 run twice: once with a personal commit skill installed, once with ~/.claude/skills/commit moved aside.

evals.name: branch-before-first-edit
evals.prompt: Fix the typo in README.md: change 'labb' to 'lab'.
evals.expected_output: A type/slug branch (fix/...) created from the fresh origin/main tip before the first edit. No edit lands on main.
expectations: git branch --show-current runs before any file edit
git fetch origin runs before the branch is created
The branch is created with git checkout -b <type>/<slug> origin/main
The branch name matches <type>/<kebab-slug> with an approved type
No Edit or Write happens while on main

evals.name: related-work-stays-on-branch
evals.prompt: (start on branch feat/orders-model with one commit) Also add a usage note to orders.sql.
evals.expected_output: The task continues on feat/orders-model. No new branch.
expectations: No new branch is created
The edit happens on feat/orders-model

evals.name: unrelated-work-branches-from-fresh-main
evals.prompt: (start on branch feat/orders-model, clean tree) Unrelated request: add a Checks section to AGENTS.md.
evals.expected_output: A new chore/ branch created from the fresh origin/main tip, not from feat/orders-model.
expectations: git fetch origin runs before the switch
The new branch starts at origin/main, not at feat/orders-model
The branch type is chore/ or another sensible type, never a reuse of feat/orders-model

evals.name: ask-when-uncommitted-changes-block
evals.prompt: (start on branch feat/orders-model with uncommitted edits) Unrelated request: fix a typo in AGENTS.md.
evals.expected_output: Claude asks whether to commit the pending edits first or bring them along, and waits. No silent stash, commit, or discard.
expectations: Claude asks the commit-first-or-bring-along question before switching
No git stash, commit, restore, or checkout runs before the user answers

evals.name: explore-verdict-and-park
evals.prompt: /test-lab-learning:explore <topic> (user chooses to park during the discussion)
evals.expected_output: A briefing (fundamentals first, repo-grounded), at most 2 questions, then a forced verdict. On park: an IDEAS.md Parked entry with problem, trigger, source, and page link. No implementation before the verdict.
expectations: No file edit outside explorations/ and IDEAS.md happens before the verdict
The briefing states the general principle before repo specifics
At most two discussion questions are asked
The exploration ends in exactly one verdict: implement now, park, or drop
On park, IDEAS.md gains an entry with problem, trigger to reconsider, source, and page link
Every verdict adds an IDEAS.md entry; on implement now or drop, the exploration page is removed and only a park verdict keeps it

evals.name: explore-page-artifact
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML page under explorations/, built by build_page.py from a briefing fragment; only the page is committed, not the fragment.
expectations: A single .html file exists under explorations/ for the concept
The page holds the briefing sections, insight callouts, and collapsed quick-check answers
The source line at the bottom links every source URL as an <a href> anchor
The page loads no external resource (no script, stylesheet, font, or image)
The briefing fragment source is not committed

evals.name: explore-url-input
evals.prompt: /test-lab-learning:explore <url> (an article that holds one out-of-date claim)
evals.expected_output: The article is read first and treated as the seed, not the authority. The reply names the core concept, verifies checkable facts against primary sources, flags the out-of-date claim, and cites the article next to the primary sources.
expectations: The reply names the core concept back to the user before the briefing
The briefing takes checkable facts from primary sources, not from the article
The reply flags where the article is out of date
The source line links the article and the primary sources
The exploration ends in exactly one verdict: implement now, park, or drop

evals.name: debrief-fires-before-commit-proposal
evals.prompt: (a task with a non-trivial diff reaches its natural stopping point)
evals.expected_output: The debrief runs before any commit proposal: a single guided opener question that asks for the user's theory of the diff, then the concept walk, then the teach-back, then the residual note, then the commit proposal.
expectations: The debrief starts before any commit split or commit message is proposed
The opener is one guided question and asks for the user's own theory of the diff
No explanation of the diff is given before the user answers the opener

evals.name: debrief-teach-back-mechanics
evals.prompt: (same run as eval 16, through the teach-back)
evals.expected_output: 2-3 teach-back questions asked one at a time, at least one a TODO(human) blank rebuilt from the shipped diff. A wrong answer gets one probing question before the correction. The close is the metacognitive question about the chosen approach.
expectations: Each message holds exactly one question, and the next question waits for the answer
At least one question is a TODO(human) blank re-presenting a real piece of the shipped diff with a gap
On a wrong or partial answer, one probing question comes before the correction is revealed
The teach-back closes with the metacognitive question about why this approach over the alternative

evals.name: debrief-note-approval
evals.prompt: (same run as eval 16, through the residual note)
evals.expected_output: A residual note synthesized from what the teach-back revealed, shown in chat, and saved to the knowledge base only after the user approves. Without a knowledge-base skill, no note is written anywhere.
expectations: The note draws on the teach-back (gaps, corrections, the user's phrasing), not on a diff summary
The note is shown in chat before any save
Nothing is saved without the user's yes
When no knowledge-base skill is available, the note is not written to any file or service

evals.name: end-of-task-hand-off-agnostic
evals.prompt: (start on branch fix/readme-typo with one uncommitted edit) Task is done. Wrap up.
evals.expected_output: Debrief runs, then one message proposes the commit split and the push, then the session waits. With a commit skill installed that skill is followed. Without one, the fallback in the flow skill proposes plain git commands. No commit or push before a yes. No PR in either case.
expectations: The debrief skill runs before any commit proposal
Exactly one message proposes the split, the messages, and the push, then the turn ends
No git commit or git push runs before the user's yes
With ~/.claude/skills/commit present, the commit skill's procedure is followed
With no commit skill present, the flow fallback is used and the subject is imperative, 65 characters max, no trailer
gh pr create never runs

evals.name: debrief-waives-a-trivial-diff
evals.prompt: (a task whose whole diff is one typo fix reaches its stopping point) Task is done. Wrap up.
evals.expected_output: One line says the diff teaches nothing, then the run continues to the commit hand-off. No opener, no concept walk, no teach-back.
expectations: The waiver is one line and names the reason (typo, rename, or version bump)
No opener question is asked
The run continues to the commit hand-off in the flow skill
